# AGENT-GUARD
**Disclosure checks · Recoverable deletion · Agent experiments** · 简体中文

Agent Guard has three main capabilities: **Exfil-guard** checks text before
sending it, **Delete-gua

rd** preserves recovery data before supported destructive
actions, and **Guard-lab** tests agent and

host behaviour through controlled
experiments. A shared Python Core supports the command-line tools

and optional
host adapters.

**AI agents setting up this project:** Before changing configuration or writing
a bridge, read the i

ntegration requirements, then
the setup workflow and
the matching adapter guide. Check your actual h

ost/version and its official
hook documentation, verify the integration, and report the observed cov

erage.
Installed Skills or copied configuration alone do not establish protection.

We currently focus on **DSH and Kimi Code** integrations. For other hosts,
ask the official coding a
gent to configure Agent Guard locally.

Version **0.2.9** makes cleanup
investigation faster: get a bounded directory overview, then measure

selected
scopes through Cleanup Copilot or MCP. Existing plan scans also reuse metadata
and Git que

ries. These observations grant no deletion permission; execution
still requires a separate reviewed

plan and confirmation.
See the workflow and limits.

## guard-lab: test with evidence

guard-lab is a **user-controlled experiment tool**. It puts non-secret,
synthetic markers and harmle

ss bait into a disposable project and observes
only declared channels. The real controller and evide

nce stay outside the
fixture given to the tested agent.
Its workflow separates three questions:

1. **Calibrate:** do the observer, markers, scans and evidence chain work?
Built-in controls call no

model and make no external-network request.
2. **Observe exposure:** does an unguarded real-harness

trial trigger the
selected channel?
3. **Compare protection:** after an effective baseline, does a

matched
guarded trial reduce or block that exposure?

A control PASS means **instrument calibration**, not model safety.
An unhealthy observer or missing

evidence is `INCONCLUSIVE`; a quiet
guard-off baseline cannot establish mitigation. Matched comparis

ons require
the same relevant harness/version/model, task, protocol and non-guard
configuration. Lab

results cover the declared channels, not every file read,
external transfer or model request. Exist

ing
Kimi and
DSH reports retain their bounded
results, failures and review states.

Since RC3, the package includes blue-team research, a
sanitized experiment report and a
portable fou

r-control example.
The research covers provenance, disclosure permissions and task utility in
bounde

d private experiments; those methods do not extend production hook
coverage. Lab proceeds gradually.
